findings.title: Payment settlement is a non-atomic check-then-act: concurrent duplicate callbacks can double-fulfill
findings.evidence: handleVnpayIpn/handleMomoIpn/confirmReturn guard duplicates only with `if (order.getStatus()==SUCCEEDED) return;` then call settle(). PaymentOrder has NO @Version, wallet repos use NO pessimistic lock (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE), and dtb_payment_callbacks has NO unique constraint on (provider, provider_txn_ref). Under READ_COMMITTED two concurrent callbacks (VNPay IPN + browser return, or MoMo IPN retry) both read status=PENDING, both pass the check, both settle().
findings.impact: Double plan activation / double credit grant (SUBSCRIPTION) or double print-order fulfillment (PRINT) from a single payment. Gateways routinely retry IPNs, so this is reachable in normal operation, not just under attack.
findings.recommendation: Make settlement atomic: (a) add a UNIQUE constraint on dtb_payment_callbacks(provider, provider_txn_ref) so a replay insert fails, and/or (b) lock the order row with a pessimistic SELECT ... FOR UPDATE (or add @Version to PaymentOrder) and re-check status inside the locked transaction before settle(). Prefer a DB-enforced idempotency key over the in-memory status check.

findings.title: JWT signing secret defaults to a publicly-known placeholder and .env still uses it
findings.evidence: app.jwt.secret defaults to 'change-me-please-use-a-long-random-secret-at-least-32-bytes' (>=32 bytes, so Keys.hmacShaKeyFor accepts it and the app boots). The committed developer .env sets JWT_SECRET=change-m... i.e. the same default. Anyone who knows this public string can forge access tokens with arbitrary `roles` claims.
findings.impact: Full authentication bypass and privilege escalation in any environment that runs with the default secret (dev today; production if the env var is ever unset). Attacker mints an admin/staff JWT and calls any authenticated endpoint.
findings.recommendation: Fail fast on boot if app.jwt.secret equals the placeholder or is unset in non-dev profiles. Generate a unique random 32+ byte secret per environment; never ship a working default. Rotate immediately if the default was ever used in a shared/deployed environment.

findings.title: Public unauthenticated PUT /api/common/3d/tasks/{id}/usdz allows overwriting any task's AR asset
findings.evidence: cacheTaskUsdz(@PathVariable UUID id, @RequestBody byte[] usdz) -> storeUsdz(id, usdz) has NO principal and NO ownership check; SecurityConfig permits PUT /api/common/3d/tasks/*/usdz for everyone. Every other MeshyController mutation correctly passes principal.getId() for ownership.
findings.impact: Any unauthenticated caller who knows/guesses a task UUID can replace that task's USDZ served to iOS Quick Look, enabling content injection / storage abuse. UUIDs are unguessable so exposure needs a leaked id, but the write is entirely unauthenticated.
findings.recommendation: Require auth + ownership for the write (accept the client-built USDZ only from the owning user), or write it server-side during export instead of trusting a public PUT. Validate content-type/size and cap storage.

findings.title: CORS allows credentials with broad origin patterns (*.vercel.app, localhost:*)
findings.evidence: corsConfigurationSource sets allowCredentials(true) with allowedOriginPatterns including https://*.vercel.app, http://localhost:5173, http://localhost:*, http://127.0.0.1:*, and multiple ngrok wildcards as the DEFAULT (used when APP_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN_PATTERNS is unset).
findings.impact: Any site hosted on *.vercel.app (i.e. anyone) becomes a permitted credentialed origin. Token auth is header-based (not cookies) which limits automatic credential replay, but the exposed Authorization header + wildcard origin is still an unnecessarily wide trust boundary.
findings.recommendation: In production restrict allowedOriginPatterns to the exact known frontend origins; do not ship localhost/ngrok/*.vercel.app defaults into prod. Consider splitting the public texture/model proxies (which need broad CORS) from credentialed API routes.

findings.title: Access AND refresh tokens stored in localStorage (XSS can exfiltrate the 7-day refresh token)
findings.evidence: tokenStore keeps innerstyle.accessToken and innerstyle.refreshToken in localStorage. Refresh TTL is 7 days (JWT_REFRESH_TTL=P7D).
findings.impact: Any XSS on the SPA can read both tokens; the long-lived refresh token gives persistent account takeover beyond the 15-minute access window.
findings.recommendation: Store the refresh token in an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookie (server-set) so JS cannot read it; keep only the short-lived access token in memory (not localStorage). Pair with a strict CSP to reduce XSS reach.

findings.title: MoMo gateway HTTP client has no timeout
findings.evidence: private final RestClient restClient = RestClient.create(); used for the create-payment POST with no connect/read timeout. (By contrast MeshyClientConfig correctly sets 10s/60s timeouts.)
findings.impact: If MoMo is slow/unresponsive the request thread blocks indefinitely; enough concurrent slow calls exhaust the servlet thread pool and stall the whole API.
findings.recommendation: Build the RestClient from a ClientHttpRequestFactory with explicit connect + read timeouts (mirror MeshyClientConfig). Add a short circuit/timeout and map failure to UpstreamServiceException (already thrown on other errors).

findings.title: Rate limiter fails open on Redis errors, disabling login/payment brute-force protection
findings.evidence: catch (RuntimeException ex) => fail-open (documented intent: 'fail-open if Redis is unavailable'). The same limiter backs login (5/min), register, email OTP and payment (5/min).
findings.impact: A Redis outage (or induced errors) silently removes rate limiting from security-sensitive endpoints, enabling credential-stuffing, OTP brute force, and payment spam.
findings.recommendation: Split the policy: fail-OPEN for benign read limits, but fail-CLOSED (or fall back to a local in-process limiter) for login / OTP / payment. Alert when the limiter degrades.

findings.title: No CI/CD pipeline: build, test, lint and deploy are manual and unverified
findings.evidence: No .github/workflows directory in either repo. Rule 17 mandates a lint/check gate, but nothing enforces it automatically. Combined with ~10 backend test files for ~182 sources and no coverage threshold.
findings.impact: Regressions (including the CRITICAL payment/auth issues above) can merge and deploy with no automated gate; releases depend on manual discipline.
findings.recommendation: Add CI running mvn verify + ESLint + Playwright on every PR, blocking merge on failure; add a coverage threshold; wire deploy from a green pipeline.

findings.title: dtb_payment_callbacks lacks a unique constraint for replay defense
findings.evidence: Table comment claims 'idempotency / replay defence' but there is only a non-unique index; no UNIQUE on (provider, provider_txn_ref) or on a gateway transaction id. dtb_payment_orders.provider_txn_ref is also only indexed, not unique.
findings.impact: The database cannot reject a replayed callback; the only defense is the racy app-level status check (see C1).
findings.recommendation: Add UNIQUE(provider, provider_txn_ref) on the callback (or order) table so duplicate gateway transactions are rejected at the DB. This directly hardens C1.

findings.title: Committed build artifacts and scratch files pollute the frontend repo
findings.evidence: ~40 vite.config.js.timestamp-*.mjs files, plus dist/, playwright-report/, test-results/, and stray _axis.mjs / _t.mjs / _test3mf.mjs / chk.cjs present in the tree.
findings.impact: Noise in diffs/reviews, larger clones, and risk of stale/generated files being edited by mistake.
findings.recommendation: Delete the timestamp/scratch files and add them (plus dist/, playwright-report/, test-results/) to .gitignore.

findings.title: i18n key parity gap between en and vi locales
findings.evidence: en.js ~616 key lines vs vi.js ~614 (751 vs 748 lines total). A small number of keys exist in one locale but not the other.
findings.impact: Missing keys fall back to raw keys or English for Vietnamese users on affected strings.
findings.recommendation: Add a build-time locale-parity check (diff key sets) and fill the missing vi keys.

findings.title: Critical paths (payments, concurrency, auth) appear untested; no coverage gate
findings.evidence: ~10 backend test files for ~182 sources; no unit test coverage measurement/threshold. Frontend has Playwright e2e but no unit tests. The C1 payment race and C2 auth issues would not be caught by a regression test today.
findings.recommendation: Prioritize tests for: idempotent settlement under concurrent callbacks, JWT secret/role enforcement, ownership guards, hold capture/release. Add coverage thresholds in CI (M6).

findings.title: Redis SSL enabled against localhost with empty password (config inconsistency)
findings.evidence: spring.data.redis.ssl.enabled: true with REDIS_HOST=localhost and REDIS_PASSWORD empty in dev.
findings.impact: Local Redis without TLS will fail to connect, or the setting is misleading across environments.
findings.recommendation: Make ssl.enabled environment-driven (false in dev, true in prod) and require a password in non-dev.

findings.title: No metrics/tracing observability for a payment + external-API system
findings.evidence: Only /actuator/health is exposed; no metrics, no request correlation id observed. The system calls a paid external API (Meshy) and processes payments.
findings.impact: Hard to detect/triage payment failures, Meshy slowness, or abuse in production.
findings.recommendation: Expose metrics (Micrometer/Prometheus), add a request/correlation id filter, and log key money/external events with it.

findings.title: VNPay signature comparison is case-sensitive exact match
findings.evidence: matches() compares lower-case hex exactly. VNPay's newer spec returns lower-case, so this is currently fine, but a gateway returning upper-case hex would be wrongly rejected.
findings.impact: Potential false-negative signature verification if the gateway hex case ever changes.
findings.recommendation: Normalize both sides to lower-case before the constant-time compare.

findings.title: Hardcoded pricing / fee magic values in application.yml
findings.evidence: app.print.fee and per-height prices are literals in yml (acceptable as config, but duplicated with DB mtb_pricing and frontend pricing.js).
findings.impact: Three sources of pricing truth (yml, DB master table, FE) can drift.
findings.recommendation: Pick one authoritative source (DB mtb_pricing) and derive the others; keep yml only as fallback.
